newsitem.title: USA: Charles Barkley testifies in Cleveland civil trial.
newsitem.headline: Charles Barkley testifies in Cleveland civil trial.

text.p: NBA All-Star basketball player Charles Barkley, testifying at his civil trial about a barroom scuffle last year, said Wednesday he did not know if he struck his accuser but wished he had.
"I don't know if I ever got to hit him but I hope I did," Barkley said stone-faced to laughs from the audience watching in Cuyahoga County Court.
"I still don't think he got what he deserved ... from me," the Houston Rockets' forward said.

An eight-person jury was hearing the third day of testimony in a lawsuit brought by Rochester, New York, native Jeb Tyler, 24, who police said ended up with blood on his face after the scuffle last July.
Tyler was seeking at least $50,000 in compensatory and punitive damages from Barkley, claiming he was hit repeatedly on the head.

Barkley contended that he and Olympic teammate Reggie Miller, in town for an exhibition game prior to the Atlanta Games, were talking with a female patron at a bar when a group of men approached, and that she informed Barkley that one of them had asked if she was sleeping with either of the players.
"I asked the man to leave a couple of times. Then he said, 'Why don't you f...... leave?' and then he took a step toward
"If you make a move toward me, I'm going to pop you," he said, adding that if he had struck Tyler, "he'd have more than those superficial rug burns."
"I would have been satisfied if he had just walked away. I have no remorse for protecting myself," he said.
Barkley, who has been fined by the NBA for spitting on a fan and other misbehaviour, was acquitted in 1992 of misdemeanor battery and disorderly conduct after a bar fight in Milwaukee.
